stem: Which statement about nursing documentation is correct?

options.A: Document assessments and care objectively, accurately, and promptly after they occur, and correct errors through the approved traceable record process.
options.B: Document planned interventions before they are performed when the nurse expects to complete them by the end of the shift.
options.C: Delete an inaccurate electronic entry so the original information is no longer visible in the record.
options.D: Limit documentation to medications and procedures because client assessments and responses are not part of the legal health record.

rationale: Current Open RN/NCBI nursing guidance states that the electronic health record is a legal document and that nursing documentation should be objective, factual, professional, accurate, and timely. Care or assessments that were not completed must never be charted as completed, and documentation should occur after the task or as close to the time of care as possible. Electronic charting errors should be corrected using the record's traceable correction process rather than erased or concealed. Therefore A is correct. B is advance/falsified charting, C destroys the audit trail, and D incorrectly excludes assessments and responses from nursing documentation.
educational_objective: Document nursing assessments, interventions, communications, and client responses accurately and promptly after care, and correct charting errors through a traceable approved process without deleting or concealing the original record.
source_document_title: Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition — Communication: Documentation; Nursing Management and Professional Concepts — Legal Implications
source_version_date: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals 2nd edition current in NCBI Bookshelf; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Nursing Fundamentals > 2.5 Documentation > Legal Documentation: EHR documentation is a legal document; objective/factual/professional; accurate and timely after task; do not chart uncompleted care; electronic errors corrected with details/correction preserved. Nursing Management and Professional Concepts > Documentation: document assessments, observations, communications and actions objectively, timely and accurately, as close to care as possible.
source_claim_supported: Nursing documentation is part of the legal health record and must be objective, accurate, timely, completed after care, and corrected through a traceable process rather than erased or prospectively falsified.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care: document client care accurately, maintain legal/professional accountability, communicate changes and interventions, and follow organizational/regulatory requirements for records.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — legal nursing documentation and record correction

source_original.stem: Which statement about nursing documentation is correct?

options.A: Document assessments and care accurately, objectively, and promptly, and correct errors through the approved traceable record process.
options.B: Document planned interventions before they are performed when the nurse expects to complete them by the end of the shift.
options.C: Delete an inaccurate electronic entry so the original information is no longer visible in the record.
options.D: Limit documentation to medications and procedures because patient responses are not part of the legal health record.

source_original.rationale: NCBI Nursing Fundamentals identifies EHR documentation as a legal document and states that entries should be objective, factual, accurate, and timely. Care not completed must not be charted as completed, and errors should be corrected using an appropriate traceable process rather than erased or concealed.
source_original.source_detail: EHR documentation is a legal document; entries must be accurate and timely Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, assignment/delegation, advocacy/client rights, continuity/referral, legal scope, professional limitations and emergency/quality-management activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the legal-documentation construct and key A, tightened the answer to specify documentation after care and traceable error correction, clarified that client assessments/responses belong in the record, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests direct legal-documentation principles.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current NCBI/Open RN nursing documentation guidance with NCSBN 2026 blueprint alignment
audit_findings.exact_locator: Nursing Fundamentals 2.5 Legal Documentation and Nursing Management Legal Implications > Documentation
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses directly supported documentation principles and avoids vendor-specific EHR correction instructions; 'approved traceable process' preserves organization-specific implementation while requiring an audit trail.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because care must not be charted before completion.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because electronic record errors should be corrected without eliminating the traceable history.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because assessments, observations, interventions, communications and client responses are part of nursing documentation.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A combines accuracy, timing, objectivity and traceable correction without violating legal documentation standards.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address documentation practices within the legal health record.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care — documentation, legal accountability and communication of care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current Open RN/NCBI legal-documentation text, all alternatives, rationale, objective, error-correction wording, ambiguity, cueing and Management of Care alignment. A remained uniquely correct.
